records.title: Typed operator grammar
records.scope: Finite vertex set, arbitrary arrow set, source/target maps, independent vector spaces and typed arrow maps; relations are finite linear combinations of paths with fixed endpoints. The more general free-algebra relation format is specialized both to homogeneous typed path relations and to all representatives of an actual TwoSidedIdeal.

records.scope: Total space is the finite product, canonically the finite direct sum. Vertex operators are single-after-projection maps and arrows are single-after-arrow-after-projection. records.title: Typed realization and module equivalence
records.scope: The grammar algebra is constructed by FreeAlgebra and RingQuot, with complete orthogonal vertex idempotents and exact source/target arrow corners. Collapse is full, faithful and essentially surjective, using actual vertex ranges and their analysis/synthesis equivalence. Action objects are then proved equivalent to ordinary ModuleCat for all unital left modules; the coefficient action is recovered through algebraMap. A separate quotient comparison uses the actual TwoSidedIdeal ring congruence and proves both inverse identities. No category equivalence, split decomposition, path action or module structure is supplied as an assumption.

records.scope: The operator hull is the scalar span of actual action values; for an acting algebra this is AS. This supplies the exact topological clause alongside the separately accepted algebraic theorem.

This supplies the exact topological clause alongside separately accepted algebraic invariance.

records.title: Nakayama lemma
records.scope: The noncommutative input is integrated at the printed finitely generated left-module scope. For any left ideal I contained in Ring.jacobson R, the actual submodule equality N ⊔ I • top = top implies N = top. No commutativity, Noetherian, semisimplicity, finite length, or two-sidedness of I is required for this lifting theorem. The proof derives the radical lifting result from maximal submodules and the ring-radical action inclusion, rather than assuming the desired conclusion.

Any lifts of a generating quotient family generate upstairs, and both minimum-cardinality inequalities are established. The natural seedFinrank equality is proved as well. No semisimplicity hypothesis is needed. The descriptive semisimple-top sentence is covered by the pinned general IsSemisimpleRing.isSemisimpleModule instance applied to this actual quotient module. This is not an algorithm for computing the radical or finding generators.

records.scope: For every division ring and positive matrix size, the natural module has canonical seed rank one and every nonzero vector generates. records.title: Multiplicity obstruction
records.scope: For arbitrary division rings and positive block size, the actual shared matrix action on m natural-module copies has canonical rank ceil(m/d). The rectangular-matrix, natural-column-product and finite-direct-sum formulations are connected by actual module equivalences. Zero multiplicity is included. This is not the independent-factor action, whose bound is a maximum across distinct factors.

records.title: Primary decomposition for polynomial modules
records.scope: For an existing polynomial module, multiplication by X constructs its evaluation operator and an actual polynomial-linear equivalence; finite coefficient dimension gives torsion. PID decomposition constructs positive elementary divisors, while actual intrinsic primary submodules are proved equal to ideal primary components. PolynomialMonic proves a bijection between monic irreducibles and nonzero prime ideals via p↦(p), deriving injectivity from monicity and surjectivity from a normalized PID prime generator. It reindexes the internal sum and finite nonzero support to precisely the manuscript index set. intrinsic_primary_finite_power_sum is a literal finite DirectSum of k[X]/(p^e), with positive e, for each specified irreducible p.

records.title: Single-operator seed rank
records.scope: The full printed statement is now mapped. The actual power-annihilation submodule is proved equal to the ideal primary component. Its inclusion into V/pV has exact kernel pX_p and is onto from the internally discharged Artinian hypothesis. The induced quotient equivalence is residue-field linear. Every intrinsic multiplicity is identified with every actual presentation fibre. The grouped factors are proved to be the literal X_p, and any positive primary decomposition of X_p has the same intrinsic count. The presentation-free maximum over all monic irreducibles is proved bounded and attained, and equals both natural-valued and cardinal-valued seed rank. No caller-supplied decomposition or seed-count conclusion is needed by the public maximum theorem. These are noncomputable mathematical constructions. The printed proof uses a different route through local-module/Nakayama machinery; that separately listed machinery is not thereby marked complete.

records.title: Invariant-factor count
records.scope: Complete at the displayed conditional scope: an actual polynomial-module equivalence to the finite product of nonconstant factors and their divisibility chain imply least seed number, natural seed rank and cardinal seed rank equal the factor count. The theorem also handles the empty product. Finite products and finite direct sums represent the same finite decomposition. Existence of an ordered invariant-factor presentation is not asserted by this declaration, and is not an additional hypothesis-free claim of the printed conditional corollary.

records.title: Geometric-multiplicity formula
records.scope: Complete at the finite-dimensional algebraically closed scope inherited from the single-operator theorem. The actual intrinsic multiplicity for X-C(a) is identified with the dimension of the actual eigenspace, without diagonalizability. The canonical natural and cardinal seed ranks equal the maximum over the actual spectrum. Off-spectrum dimensions are zero, the empty-spectrum/zero-space maximum is defined as zero, and the spectral maximum is attained on nonzero spaces. No executable spectral algorithm is claimed.

records.title: Cyclic-matrix criterion
records.scope: Block 06 closes the exact six-way criterion for a nonzero finite-dimensional operator over an arbitrary field. The final List.TFAE includes actual cyclicity, canonical seed rank one, cyclicity of every nonzero intrinsic primary component, an actual monic positive-degree one-invariant-factor presentation, minpoly=charpoly, and one-dimensional eigenspaces at every spectral value of the literal tensor extension to AlgebraicClosure k. Minimal-polynomial preservation and cyclicity preservation/descent are proved, not supplied as hypotheses. The one-factor presentation has a constructed basis in which the original operator is the standard companion matrix; its factor is proved to be the minimal polynomial. A separate theorem proves that any actual nonconstant invariant-factor chain has exactly one factor iff the operator is cyclic. This is a mathematical existence and equivalence theorem, not an executable normal-form algorithm or a full sorted invariant-factor construction for arbitrary noncyclic operators. The nonzero-space guard is retained in the six-way statement. Legacy conditional wrappers are preserved unchanged for compatibility, but the new public criterion needs no decomposition, multiplicity, polynomial-preservation, spectral, or seed-number certificates.

records.search_text: Fix an admissible arithmetic class. Suppose: item every object has a unique residual root in an exhaustive residual moduli space; item a common algebraic spine is defined for the desired system; item every coefficient-prime residual companion exists; item every companion forest has nonempty finite levels, finite branching, and inverse-limit closed local conditions; item the required horizontal transports preserve the common spine and the selected local deformation conditions. If, in addition, the system is a summand of a known compatible carrier, the summand is recovered at every coefficient prime by finitely many Frobenius traces.

records.search_text: Fix a characteristic zero deformation point (x:R to E'). Give (E') a Hausdorff topological field structure. The conditional argument uses the following five gates. item Residual gate. Residual occupancy in the declared automorphic carrier and representability of the chosen deformation problem are supplied arithmetic inputs. In particular, the deformation ring (R) and its universal representation ( rho _R) are available. item Patching gate. An applicable patching theorem supplies an ordinary finite module or a perfect complex with full patched support, together with the coefficient quotient and the module or derived control isomorphism. Write (M) for the resulting finite level carrier over (R). item Comparison gate. Let (H) be a finite ordinary Hecke module or a perfect Hecke complex over ( TT ). Supply a ring map (f:R to TT ) satisfying [ (f^*)^-1 bigl ( Supp _R(M) bigr ) subseteq Supp _ TT (H). ] Use ordinary or derived support according to the carrier. Actual scalar extension satisfies this inclusion, as does transport through a ring isomorphism with the corresponding carrier identification. item Fiber gate. Supply a Hecke point (y: TT to E') with (y circ f=x). Then the fiber of (H) at (y) is nonzero. It contains a nonzero Hecke eigenvector, in some integer cohomological degree in the derived case, with character (y). item Realization gate. The declared classicality theorem applies to the resulting eigensystem and supplies an occurring classical automorphic representation ( pi ), with a continuous semisimple attached representation. Require the specialization ( rho _x=x circ rho _R) to be continuous and supply its semisimplification. On the same Chebotarev dense set, assume that the characteristic polynomials of both ( rho _x) and the attached representation are (y(P_v(X))). Retain the standard density and general Brauer Nesbitt inputs of cref fact:chebotarev_brauer_nesbitt. Then ( rho _x^ss) is isomorphic to the representation attached to ( pi ). If ( rho _x) is irreducible, the same conclusion holds for ( rho _x) itself. For propagation, suppose both a semisimple compatible family ( rho _ lambda ) containing ( rho _x) and a family ( rho _ pi , lambda ) attached to this same ( pi ) already exist. Require the distinguished members to be ( rho _x) and its attached representation, respectively. Assume the coefficient, continuity, density, semisimplification and common algebraic Frobenius spine hypotheses of cref thm:one_member_propagation, with that spine agreeing with the specialized Hecke polynomials at the distinguished place. Then [ rho _ lambda cong rho _ pi , lambda ^ss qquad for every lambda . ]
